strings.b-00-meta.title: Motion in a Straight Line
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.0: After this lesson you can describe motion along a straight line using position, velocity and acceleration.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.1: After this lesson you can read velocity and acceleration from position-time and velocity-time graphs.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.2: After this lesson you can use the kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion and for free fall.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.3: After this lesson you can distinguish average speed from magnitude of average velocity and explain relative motion with a frame of reference.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.0.definition: Location of an object with respect to a chosen origin; to the right is positive and to the left is negative for motion in a straight line.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.1.definition: Rate of change of position with time at an instant, v = dx/dt; it has magnitude and direction.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.2.definition: Rate of change of velocity with time, a = dv/dt; it has magnitude and direction and its unit is m s-2.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.3.definition: Change in position over a time interval; it can be positive, negative or zero and equals the area under the velocity-time graph.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.4.definition: Total path length divided by the time interval; it is greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.5.definition: The fixed point or group of points with respect to which motion is measured.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.0: You see motion all around you. You walk, you run, and you ride a bicycle. Leaves fall from trees and water flows down a dam.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.1: Motion means change in position of an object with time. To describe it, you first choose an origin. Position to the right of the origin is taken as positive and to the left as negative.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.2: In this lesson we study motion along a straight line. This is called rectilinear motion. We treat objects as point objects when their size is much smaller than the distance they move.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.3: Kinematics is the study of ways to describe motion. It does not go into the causes of motion. We develop velocity and acceleration to describe how position changes with time.
strings.b-02.caption: A straight line with origin O, positive direction to the right, and a point object at position x.
strings.b-03.question: A railway carriage moves without jerks between two stations, much farther than its own length. Can it be treated as a point object?
strings.b-03.options.0: Yes, because its size is much smaller than the distance moved
strings.b-03.options.1: No, because it is a large object
strings.b-03.options.2: Yes, because it moves on a straight line
strings.b-03.options.3: No, because it has many parts
strings.b-03.explanation: An object can be treated as a point object when its size is much smaller than the distance it moves in a reasonable time.
strings.b-04.paragraphs.0: Average velocity tells you how fast an object moved over a whole interval. It does not tell you how fast it moved at one instant.
strings.b-04.paragraphs.1: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocity as the time interval becomes infinitesimally small. In symbols, v = dx/dt.
strings.b-04.paragraphs.2: On a position-time graph, velocity at an instant is the slope of the tangent at that point. Smaller intervals make the joining line approach the tangent.
strings.b-04.paragraphs.3: For x = 0.08 t^3, the average velocity centred at t = 4.0 s approaches 3.84 m s-1 as the interval decreases. That limiting value is the velocity at t = 4.0 s.
strings.b-05.title: Position-time graph and tangent slope
strings.b-05.description: Shows the curve x = 0.08 t^3 and the tangent at a chosen time. The slope of the tangent is the instantaneous velocity.
strings.b-05.controls.t.label: Time t (s)
strings.b-06.problem: The position of an object moving along x-axis is given by x = a + b t^2 where a = 8.5 m, b = 2.5 m s-2 and t is measured in seconds. What is its velocity at t = 0 s and t = 2.0 s? What is the average velocity between t = 2.0 s and t = 4.0 s?
strings.b-06.steps.0.title: Differentiate position
strings.b-06.steps.0.detail: v = dx/dt = 2 b t = 5.0 t m s-1.
strings.b-06.steps.1.title: Velocity at t = 0 s
strings.b-06.steps.2.title: Velocity at t = 2.0 s
strings.b-06.steps.3.title: Average velocity between 2.0 s and 4.0 s
strings.b-06.answer: Velocity at t = 0 s is 0 m s-1, at t = 2.0 s is 10 m s-1, and average velocity between 2.0 s and 4.0 s is 15 m s-1.
strings.b-07.paragraphs.0: Speed is the magnitude of velocity. A velocity of +24.0 m s-1 and a velocity of -24.0 m s-1 both have a speed of 24.0 m s-1.
strings.b-07.paragraphs.1: Average speed over a finite interval is greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity. But instantaneous speed at an instant is equal to the magnitude of instantaneous velocity at that instant.
strings.b-08.paragraphs.0: Velocity changes during motion. We describe this change as rate of change of velocity with time. This rate is acceleration.
strings.b-08.paragraphs.1: Average acceleration is a = (v2 - v1)/(t2 - t1), with SI unit m s-2. Instantaneous acceleration is a = dv/dt, the slope of the tangent to the velocity-time curve.
strings.b-08.paragraphs.2: Acceleration can be positive, negative or zero. It can come from a change in speed, a change in direction, or both.
strings.b-08.paragraphs.3: Position-time graphs curve upward for positive acceleration, downward for negative acceleration, and are straight lines for zero acceleration.
strings.b-09.title: Velocity-time graph and area as displacement
strings.b-09.description: Shows a velocity-time line for constant acceleration and shades the area under it. The shaded area equals displacement.
strings.b-09.controls.v0.label: Initial velocity v0 (m/s)
strings.b-09.controls.a.label: Acceleration a (m/s^2)
strings.b-10.paragraphs.0: If a particle is speeding up, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If its speed is decreasing, acceleration is in the direction opposite to velocity.
strings.b-10.paragraphs.1: This is true whatever origin and positive direction you choose. The sign of acceleration alone does not tell you if speed is increasing or decreasing.
strings.b-11.paragraphs.0: For constant acceleration, average acceleration equals the constant value during the interval. If velocity is v0 at t = 0 and v at time t, then v = v0 + a t.
strings.b-11.paragraphs.1: The area under the velocity-time graph is a triangle plus a rectangle. This area equals displacement.
strings.b-11.paragraphs.2: This gives x = ((v0 + v)/2) t, so average velocity is the arithmetic average of initial and final velocities.
strings.b-11.paragraphs.3: Eliminating t gives the three kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion.
strings.b-12.title: Deriving kinematic equations from the velocity-time area
strings.b-12.steps.0.title: Start with v = v0 + a t
strings.b-12.steps.0.detail: This comes from a = (v - v0)/t for constant acceleration.
strings.b-12.steps.1.title: Find area under v-t graph
strings.b-12.steps.1.detail: Area = area of triangle + area of rectangle = (1/2)(v - v0) t + v0 t = ((v0 + v)/2) t.
strings.b-12.steps.2.title: Area equals displacement
strings.b-12.steps.3.title: Eliminate t
strings.b-12.steps.3.detail: Use t = (v - v0)/a in x = ((v0 + v)/2) t to get v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x. Use v - v0 = a t in x = ((v0 + v)/2) t to get x = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2.
strings.b-13.title: Deriving equations of motion by calculus
strings.b-13.steps.0.title: Integrate acceleration
strings.b-13.steps.0.detail: a = dv/dt, so dv = a dt. Integrating gives v - v0 = a t, so v = v0 + a t.
strings.b-13.steps.1.title: Integrate velocity
strings.b-13.steps.1.detail: v = dx/dt, so dx = v dt. Integrating with v = v0 + a t gives x - x0 = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2.
strings.b-13.steps.2.title: Eliminate time
strings.b-13.steps.2.detail: From a = dv/dt and v = dx/dt, a = v dv/dx, so v dv = a dx. Integrating gives (1/2)(v^2 - v0^2) = a (x - x0), so v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a (x - x0).
strings.b-14.problem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 20 m s-1 from the top of a multistorey building. The height of the point from where the ball is thrown is 25.0 m from the ground. (a) How high will the ball rise? and (b) how long will it be before the ball hits the ground? Take g = 10 m s-2.
strings.b-14.steps.0.title: Choose upward as positive
strings.b-14.steps.0.detail: v0 = +20 m s-1, a = -g = -10 m s-2, and at the top v = 0 m s-1.
strings.b-14.steps.1.title: Height risen
strings.b-14.steps.1.detail: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a (y - y0): 0 = (20)^2 + 2(-10)(y - y0), so y - y0 = 20 m. Height from ground is 25.0 + 20 = 45 m.
strings.b-14.steps.2.title: Time to go up
strings.b-14.steps.2.detail: Use v = v0 + a t: 0 = 20 - 10 t1, so t1 = 2 s.
strings.b-14.steps.3.title: Time to fall down
strings.b-14.answer: (a) The ball rises 20 m above the launch point, 45 m from the ground. (b) It hits the ground after 5 s.
strings.b-15.paragraphs.0: Free fall is motion under gravity with air resistance neglected. Near the earth's surface g is constant at 9.8 m s-2 when the height is small compared to the earth's radius.
strings.b-15.paragraphs.1: Take upward as positive. Then acceleration due to gravity is a = -g = -9.8 m s-2.
strings.b-15.paragraphs.2: For an object released from rest at y = 0, the kinematic equations give v = -9.8 t, y = -4.9 t^2 and v^2 = -19.6 y.
strings.b-15.paragraphs.3: Acceleration is constant, velocity varies linearly with time, and distance varies as t^2.
strings.b-16.problem: Discuss the motion of an object under free fall. Neglect air resistance. Take g = 9.8 m s-2, upward positive, released from rest at y = 0.
strings.b-16.steps.0.title: Write acceleration
strings.b-16.steps.1.title: Velocity with time
strings.b-16.steps.2.title: Position with time
strings.b-16.steps.3.title: Velocity with position
strings.b-17.problem: Galileo's law of odd numbers: The distances traversed, during equal intervals of time, by a body falling from rest, stand to one another in the same ratio as the odd numbers beginning with unity, namely 1:3:5:7. Prove it.
strings.b-17.steps.0.title: Use free-fall position
strings.b-17.steps.0.detail: For fall from rest, position magnitude is (1/2) g t^2.
strings.b-17.steps.1.title: Take equal intervals
strings.b-17.steps.1.detail: Divide time into equal intervals of length tau and find positions after tau, 2 tau, 3 tau and so on.
strings.b-17.steps.2.title: Find distances in successive intervals
strings.b-17.steps.2.detail: Subtract successive positions. The distances are in the ratio 1:3:5:7:9:11 and so on.
strings.b-17.answer: Distances in successive equal time intervals are in the ratio 1:3:5:7:9:11, proving the law of odd numbers.
strings.b-18.problem: When brakes are applied to a moving vehicle, the distance it travels before stopping is called stopping distance. Derive an expression for stopping distance in terms of v0 and a, where a is the deceleration caused by braking.
strings.b-18.steps.0.title: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x
strings.b-18.steps.0.detail: Let stopping distance be ds and final velocity v = 0.
strings.b-18.steps.1.title: Solve for ds
strings.b-18.steps.2.title: Interpret the result
strings.b-18.steps.2.detail: Stopping distance is proportional to v0^2. Doubling v0 increases ds by a factor of 4 for the same deceleration.
strings.b-18.answer: Stopping distance ds = -v0^2/(2 a), proportional to the square of initial velocity.
strings.b-19.problem: Reaction time is the time a person takes to observe, think and act. A ruler is dropped vertically and caught after travelling d = 21.0 cm. Estimate the reaction time. Take g = 9.8 m s-2.
strings.b-19.steps.0.title: Use free fall
strings.b-19.steps.0.detail: The ruler drops from rest, so distance magnitude is (1/2) g t_r^2.
strings.b-19.steps.1.title: Insert d
strings.b-19.steps.2.title: Solve for t_r
strings.b-20.paragraphs.0: For uniform motion, acceleration is zero. The x-t graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis and the v-t graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis.
strings.b-20.paragraphs.1: For uniform acceleration, the x-t graph is a parabola and the v-t graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis.
strings.b-20.paragraphs.2: Choose the origin and positive direction before assigning signs. The sign of acceleration alone does not tell whether speed increases or decreases.
strings.b-20.paragraphs.3: Zero velocity at an instant does not mean zero acceleration. Kinematic equations apply only when acceleration magnitude and direction are constant, with values substituted with proper signs.
strings.b-21.question: Which statement is true for one-dimensional motion?
strings.b-21.options.0: Zero speed at an instant may have non-zero acceleration at that instant
strings.b-21.options.1: Zero speed may have non-zero velocity
strings.b-21.options.2: Constant speed must have zero acceleration
strings.b-21.options.3: Positive acceleration must mean speeding up
strings.b-21.explanation: A particle thrown up has zero velocity at the top but gravity acceleration continues. Zero speed means zero velocity magnitude, constant speed can still have acceleration from direction change, and positive acceleration depends on the chosen positive direction.
strings.b-22.problem: A car moving along a straight highway with speed of 126 km h-1 is brought to a stop within a distance of 200 m. What is the retardation of the car (assumed uniform), and how long does it take for the car to stop?
strings.b-22.steps.0.title: Convert speed
strings.b-22.steps.0.detail: 126 km h-1 = 35 m s-1. Final velocity v = 0, distance x = 200 m.
strings.b-22.steps.1.title: Find retardation
strings.b-22.steps.1.detail: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x: 0 = (35)^2 + 2 a (200), so a = -3.06 m s-2. Retardation is 3.06 m s-2.
strings.b-22.steps.2.title: Find time
strings.b-22.steps.2.detail: Use v = v0 + a t: 0 = 35 - 3.06 t, so t = 11.4 s approximately.
strings.b-22.answer: Retardation is about 3.06 m s-2 and the car stops in about 11.4 s.
strings.b-23.problem: A player throws a ball upwards with an initial speed of 29.4 m s-1. (a) What is the direction of acceleration during upward motion? (b) What are velocity and acceleration at the highest point? (d) To what height does the ball rise and after how long does it return to the player's hands? Take g = 9.8 m s-2 and neglect air resistance.
strings.b-23.steps.0.title: Direction of acceleration
strings.b-23.steps.0.detail: Acceleration due to gravity is downward during upward motion.
strings.b-23.steps.1.title: At highest point
strings.b-23.steps.1.detail: Velocity is zero, acceleration is still downward with magnitude 9.8 m s-2.
strings.b-23.steps.2.title: Height risen
strings.b-23.steps.2.detail: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x with upward positive: 0 = (29.4)^2 + 2(-9.8) h, so h = 44.1 m.
strings.b-23.steps.3.title: Time to return
strings.b-23.steps.3.detail: Time up = 29.4/9.8 = 3 s. By symmetry time down is also 3 s, so total time is 6 s.
strings.b-23.answer: Acceleration is downward, velocity at the top is zero with downward acceleration 9.8 m s-2, height risen is 44.1 m, and return time is 6 s.
strings.b-24.problem: A drunkard walking in a narrow lane takes 5 steps forward and 3 steps backward, followed again by 5 steps forward and 3 steps backward, and so on. Each step is 1 m long and requires 1 s. How long does he take to fall in a pit 13 m away from the start?
strings.b-24.steps.0.title: Plot motion
strings.b-24.steps.0.detail: Each forward step has slope +1 m/s and each backward step has slope -1 m/s on an x-t graph.
strings.b-24.steps.1.title: Track position
strings.b-24.steps.1.detail: After first 5 forward: 5 m at 5 s. After 3 back: 2 m at 8 s. After next 5 forward: 7 m at 13 s. After 3 back: 4 m at 16 s. After next 5 forward: 9 m at 21 s. After 3 back: 6 m at 24 s. After next 5 forward: 11 m at 29 s. After 3 back: 8 m at 32 s.
strings.b-24.steps.2.title: Reach the pit
strings.b-24.steps.2.detail: Next 5 forward steps take him from 8 m to 13 m, reaching the pit at 37 s.
strings.b-24.answer: He falls in the pit after 37 s.
strings.b-25.question: A woman walks from home to an office 2.5 km away, stays at the office for a long time, then returns home by auto. What does the x-t graph look like during her stay at the office?
strings.b-25.options.0: A horizontal line, because position does not change and velocity is zero
strings.b-25.options.1: A steep upward line, because she is at the office
strings.b-25.options.2: A steep downward line, because she will return later
strings.b-25.options.3: A parabola, because time is passing
strings.b-25.explanation: During the stay, position is constant, so the x-t graph is horizontal and its slope, velocity, is zero. Walking to the office gives a positive slope and returning gives a negative slope.
strings.b-26.problem: A man walks on a straight road from his home to a market 2.5 km away with a speed of 5 km h-1. Finding the market closed, he instantly turns and walks back home with a speed of 7.5 km h-1. What is the magnitude of average velocity and average speed over (i) 0 to 30 min, (ii) 0 to 50 min, (iii) 0 to 40 min?
strings.b-26.steps.0.title: Time to market
strings.b-26.steps.0.detail: 2.5 km at 5 km h-1 takes 0.5 h = 30 min.
strings.b-26.steps.1.title: 0 to 30 min
strings.b-26.steps.1.detail: Displacement = 2.5 km, path = 2.5 km. Magnitude of average velocity = 2.5/0.5 = 5 km h-1. Average speed = 5 km h-1.
strings.b-26.steps.2.title: 0 to 50 min
strings.b-26.steps.2.detail: In 20 min back at 7.5 km h-1 he covers 2.5 km and reaches home. Displacement = 0, so magnitude of average velocity = 0. Path = 5 km in 50 min, average speed = 6 km h-1.
strings.b-26.steps.3.title: 0 to 40 min
strings.b-26.steps.3.detail: In 10 min back he covers 1.25 km, so position from home is 1.25 km. Magnitude of average velocity = 1.25/(2/3) = 1.875 km h-1. Path = 3.75 km, average speed = 3.75/(2/3) = 5.625 km h-1.
strings.b-26.answer: (i) 5 km h-1 and 5 km h-1. (ii) 0 km h-1 and 6 km h-1. (iii) 1.875 km h-1 and 5.625 km h-1.
strings.b-27.question: For one-dimensional motion, how do magnitude of displacement and total path length compare over an interval?
strings.b-27.options.0: Total path length is greater than or equal to magnitude of displacement, with equality only when there is no turning back
strings.b-27.options.1: Magnitude of displacement is always greater than path length
strings.b-27.explanation: Displacement depends only on start and end positions, while path length adds every step. Turning back makes path length larger. The same holds for average speed versus magnitude of average velocity.
strings.b-28.question: Two children A and B return from school on x-t graphs. A starts at t = 0 with a smaller slope, B starts later with a larger slope, and both end at the same home position. Which conclusion follows?
strings.b-28.options.0: B walks faster because slope is larger, even though B starts later
strings.b-28.options.1: A walks faster because A starts earlier
strings.b-28.options.2: Both walk at the same speed because they end together
strings.b-28.options.3: Speed cannot be read from an x-t graph
strings.b-28.explanation: Slope of an x-t graph is velocity. Larger slope means larger speed. The intercept on the time axis shows start time, and the final position shows distance from school.
strings.b-29.question: A ball is dropped from a height of 90 m and at each collision with the floor loses one tenth of its speed. What will its speed-time graph between t = 0 and 12 s look like?
strings.b-29.options.0: Speed increases linearly during each fall, then drops suddenly at each bounce to nine tenths of the previous impact speed, with smaller peaks each time
strings.b-29.options.2: Speed decreases linearly to zero and stays zero
strings.b-29.options.3: Speed increases without any drop at bounces
strings.b-29.explanation: During free fall speed increases with time. At collision speed falls to nine tenths, so the next peak is smaller. Velocity and acceleration cannot change abruptly in a realistic smooth graph, but speed drops at the bounce in this idealised description.
strings.b-30.question: Which of these cannot possibly represent one-dimensional motion of a particle?
strings.b-30.options.0: An x-t graph with a vertical segment, implying infinite velocity at one instant
strings.b-30.options.1: An x-t graph that is a straight inclined line
strings.b-30.options.2: A v-t graph that is a straight inclined line
strings.b-30.options.3: An x-t graph that is a parabola for constant acceleration
strings.b-30.explanation: A vertical x-t segment would mean position changes in zero time, giving infinite velocity. Straight inclined x-t, inclined v-t and parabolic x-t are all possible for uniform or uniformly accelerated motion.
strings.b-31.question: An x-t graph is a straight line for t < 0 and a parabola for t > 0. Is it correct to say the particle moves in a straight line for t < 0 and on a parabolic path for t > 0?
strings.b-31.options.0: No. The graph plots position against time; the particle still moves on a straight line, and the parabola means position varies as t^2 due to acceleration
strings.b-31.options.1: Yes, the shape of the graph is the path of the particle
strings.b-31.options.2: Yes, for t > 0 the particle leaves the straight line
strings.b-31.options.3: No, because x-t graphs cannot be parabolas
strings.b-31.explanation: An x-t graph is not a trajectory in space. For one-dimensional motion the particle moves on a straight line; a parabolic x-t graph indicates constant acceleration.
strings.b-32.paragraphs.0: Motion is always measured with respect to a fixed point. This fixed point is called a frame of reference.
strings.b-32.paragraphs.1: The choice of point is arbitrary and all frames of reference are equally valid. A passenger in a moving car is not moving with respect to the driver.
strings.b-32.paragraphs.2: Both passenger and driver are moving for a person on the sidewalk. Relative velocity compares motion seen from different frames.
strings.b-32.paragraphs.3: To find the speed relevant for one object hitting another, you compare their velocities in the same frame of reference.
strings.b-33.problem: A police van moving on a highway with a speed of 30 km h-1 fires a bullet at a thief's car speeding away in the same direction with a speed of 192 km h-1. If the muzzle speed of the bullet is 150 m s-1, with what speed does the bullet hit the thief's car?
strings.b-33.steps.0.title: Convert speeds to m s-1
strings.b-33.steps.1.title: Bullet speed with respect to ground
strings.b-33.steps.1.detail: Bullet speed = muzzle speed + van speed = 150 + 8.33 = 158.33 m s-1 in the same direction.
strings.b-33.steps.2.title: Speed relative to thief's car
strings.b-33.steps.2.detail: Relative speed = 158.33 - 53.33 = 105 m s-1. This is the speed relevant for damaging the thief's car.
strings.b-33.answer: The bullet hits the thief's car with a relative speed of about 105 m s-1.
strings.b-34.question: A passenger sits in a moving car. With respect to whom is the passenger moving?
strings.b-34.options.0: Not moving with respect to the driver, but moving with respect to a person on the sidewalk
strings.b-34.options.1: Moving with respect to the driver but not with respect to the sidewalk
strings.b-34.options.2: Not moving with respect to anyone
strings.b-34.options.3: Moving with respect to the car seat only
strings.b-34.explanation: Motion is relative to a frame of reference. The passenger and driver share the same frame, while the sidewalk person is in a different frame.
strings.b-35.question: A velocity-time graph rises with a constant slope, then becomes horizontal, then falls with a constant slope to zero. What physical situation does it suggest?
strings.b-35.options.0: Speeding up with constant acceleration, then moving at constant velocity, then braking to stop
strings.b-35.explanation: Slope of v-t graph is acceleration. Rising slope means positive acceleration, horizontal means zero acceleration, and falling slope means negative acceleration while still moving forward until velocity reaches zero.
strings.b-36.question: On an x-t graph at a chosen instant, position is positive and the tangent slope is negative. What are the signs of position and velocity at that instant?
strings.b-36.explanation: Position sign is read from the value of x. Velocity sign is read from the slope of the tangent; a negative slope means velocity is negative.
strings.b-37.question: An x-t graph shows three equal time intervals. The middle interval has the steepest slope, the first interval has a moderate slope, and the last interval has the shallowest slope, all with positive slope. In which interval is average speed greatest and least?
strings.b-37.options.0: Greatest in the middle interval and least in the last interval
strings.b-37.options.1: Greatest in the last interval and least in the middle interval
strings.b-37.options.2: Greatest in the first interval and least in the middle interval
strings.b-37.explanation: Average speed over an interval is magnitude of displacement divided by time, which for a straight segment is the magnitude of slope. Steepest slope gives greatest average speed and shallowest gives least. All average velocities are positive because slopes are positive.
strings.b-38.question: A speed-time graph for motion in a constant direction shows three equal time intervals. The first interval has the steepest rising slope, the second is horizontal, and the third has a shallow falling slope. In which interval is average acceleration greatest in magnitude and average speed greatest?
strings.b-38.options.0: Average acceleration greatest in the first interval; average speed greatest in the second interval if its speed level is highest
strings.b-38.options.1: Average acceleration greatest in the second interval; average speed greatest in the first interval
strings.b-38.options.2: Average acceleration greatest in the third interval; average speed greatest in the third interval
strings.b-38.options.3: Average acceleration is zero in all intervals
strings.b-38.explanation: Average acceleration is slope of speed-time graph, so steepest slope gives greatest magnitude. Average speed is average height of the graph over the interval, so the interval with highest speed level gives greatest average speed. With positive direction as motion direction, velocity is positive in all intervals and acceleration is positive, zero, then negative.
strings.b-39.paragraphs.0: Remember the three kinematic equations: v = v0 + a t, x = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2, and v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x.
strings.b-39.paragraphs.1: Use (x - x0) if the particle starts at x0. Substitute values with proper signs after choosing origin and positive direction.
strings.b-39.paragraphs.2: For free fall with upward positive, use a = -9.8 m s-2. For stopping, remember distance grows as the square of initial velocity.
strings.b-39.paragraphs.3: Read graphs carefully: slope of x-t is velocity, slope of v-t is acceleration, and area under v-t is displacement.
strings.b-40.question: An object falls freely from rest. Using y = -4.9 t^2 with upward positive, what is the magnitude of distance fallen in 2 s? Give the answer in metres.
strings.b-40.explanation: Magnitude of y = 4.9 x (2)^2 = 4.9 x 4 = 19.6 m. The negative sign shows displacement is downward when upward is positive.
strings.b-41.question: Why is there no distinction between instantaneous speed and magnitude of instantaneous velocity, while average speed can differ from magnitude of average velocity?
strings.b-41.options.0: At an instant there is no interval over which direction can change, so speed is just the magnitude of velocity at that instant
strings.b-41.options.1: Because speed is always zero at an instant
strings.b-41.options.2: Because average velocity is always zero
strings.b-41.options.3: Because instantaneous velocity has no direction
strings.b-41.explanation: Instantaneous speed is defined as the magnitude of instantaneous velocity. Average speed uses total path length over a finite interval, which can exceed the magnitude of average velocity when direction changes.
strings.b-42.question: A particle is speeding up. What is the direction of its acceleration relative to its velocity?
strings.b-42.explanation: If a particle is speeding up, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If speed is decreasing, acceleration is opposite to velocity. This is independent of the choice of origin and axis.

lesson.title: Motion in a Straight Line
objectives: After this lesson you can describe motion along a straight line using position, velocity and acceleration.
After this lesson you can read velocity and acceleration from position-time and velocity-time graphs.
After this lesson you can use the kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion and for free fall.
After this lesson you can distinguish average speed from magnitude of average velocity and explain relative motion with a frame of reference.

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: You see motion all around you. You walk, you run, and you ride a bicycle. Leaves fall from trees and water flows down a dam.
Motion means change in position of an object with time. To describe it, you first choose an origin. Position to the right of the origin is taken as positive and to the left as negative.
In this lesson we study motion along a straight line. This is called rectilinear motion. We treat objects as point objects when their size is much smaller than the distance they move.
Kinematics is the study of ways to describe motion. It does not go into the causes of motion. We develop the ideas of velocity and acceleration to describe how position changes with time.

sections.title: Instantaneous Velocity and Speed
paragraphs: Average velocity tells you how fast an object moved over a whole time interval. It does not tell you how fast it moved at one instant inside that interval.

Instantaneous velocity, or simply velocity, is the limit of average velocity as the time interval becomes infinitesimally small. In symbols, v = dx/dt. It is the rate of change of position with respect to time at that instant.

On a position-time graph, velocity at an instant is the slope of the tangent at that point. As you take smaller and smaller intervals around the instant, the line joining the two points becomes the tangent.
Speed is the magnitude of velocity. A velocity of +24.0 m s-1 and a velocity of -24.0 m s-1 both have speed 24.0 m s-1. Instantaneous speed always equals the magnitude of instantaneous velocity.

sections.title: Acceleration
paragraphs: Velocity changes during motion. We describe this change as rate of change of velocity with time. This rate is called acceleration.
Average acceleration over an interval is a = (v2 - v1)/(t2 - t1). Its SI unit is m s-2. Instantaneous acceleration is a = dv/dt, the slope of the tangent to the velocity-time curve.

Acceleration can be positive, negative or zero. It can come from a change in speed, a change in direction, or both. Position-time graphs curve upward for positive acceleration and downward for negative acceleration.
The area under a velocity-time curve between two times equals the displacement in that interval. For constant velocity u, the area is a rectangle of height u and base T, giving displacement uT.

sections.title: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion
paragraphs: In this lesson we restrict ourselves to constant acceleration. Then average acceleration equals the constant value of acceleration during the interval.
If velocity is v0 at t = 0 and v at time t, then v = v0 + a t. The area under the velocity-time graph is a triangle plus a rectangle. This gives displacement x = ((v0 + v)/2) t.
From these relations we obtain three equations: v = v0 + a t, x = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2, and v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x. They connect displacement, time, initial velocity, final velocity and acceleration.

If the particle starts at position x0 instead of zero, replace x by (x - x0). The equations are algebraic, so you must substitute values with proper signs after choosing the origin and positive direction.

sections.title: Free Fall, Stopping and Reaction
paragraphs: Free fall is motion under gravity with air resistance neglected. Near the earth's surface, if the height is small compared to the earth's radius, g is constant at 9.8 m s-2.
Take upward as positive. Then acceleration due to gravity is a = -g = -9.8 m s-2. For an object released from rest at y = 0, the equations become v = -9.8 t, y = -4.9 t^2 and v^2 = -19.6 y.

When brakes are applied, stopping distance depends on initial velocity and deceleration. It is proportional to the square of initial velocity, so doubling velocity makes stopping distance four times larger for the same deceleration.
Reaction time is the time to observe, think and act. A dropped ruler travels under free fall, so the distance it falls before you catch it can be used to estimate your reaction time.

sections.title: Relative Velocity and Points to Ponder
paragraphs: Motion is always measured with respect to a fixed point. This fixed point is called a frame of reference. The choice of point is arbitrary and all frames are equally valid.
A passenger in a moving car is not moving with respect to the driver, but both are moving for a person on the sidewalk. Relative velocity compares motion seen from different frames.
Choose the origin and positive direction before assigning signs. If a particle speeds up, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If speed decreases, acceleration is opposite to velocity.

Zero velocity at an instant does not mean zero acceleration. A particle thrown up is momentarily at rest at the top, yet gravity acceleration continues. The sign of acceleration alone does not tell you if speed is increasing or decreasing.

glossary.definition: Location of an object with respect to a chosen origin; to the right is positive and to the left is negative for motion in a straight line.
Rate of change of position with time at an instant, v = dx/dt; it has magnitude and direction.
Rate of change of velocity with time, a = dv/dt; it has magnitude and direction and its unit is m s-2.
Change in position over a time interval; it can be positive, negative or zero and equals the area under the velocity-time graph.
Total path length divided by the time interval; it is greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity.
The fixed point or group of points with respect to which motion is measured.

spec.question: A railway carriage moves without jerks between two stations, much farther than its own length. Can it be treated as a point object?
options: Yes, because its size is much smaller than the distance moved
No, because it is a large object
Yes, because it moves on a straight line
No, because it has many parts
spec.explanation: An object can be treated as a point object when its size is much smaller than the distance it moves in a reasonable time.
spec.expected_understanding: Point object approximation depends on size compared with distance moved.

paragraphs: Average velocity tells you how fast an object moved over a whole interval. It does not tell you how fast it moved at one instant.
Instantaneous velocity is the limit of average velocity as the time interval becomes infinitesimally small. In symbols, v = dx/dt.
On a position-time graph, velocity at an instant is the slope of the tangent at that point. Smaller intervals make the joining line approach the tangent.
For x = 0.08 t^3, the average velocity centred at t = 4.0 s approaches 3.84 m s-1 as the interval decreases. That limiting value is the velocity at t = 4.0 s.

spec.title: Position-time graph and tangent slope
spec.description: Shows the curve x = 0.08 t^3 and the tangent at a chosen time. The slope of the tangent is the instantaneous velocity.
spec.learning_goal: Read instantaneous velocity as the slope of the tangent to a position-time graph.
spec.default_behaviour: Shows the position-time curve with a tangent line at t = 4 s and a readout of velocity approaching 3.84 m s-1.

spec.problem: The position of an object moving along x-axis is given by x = a + b t^2 where a = 8.5 m, b = 2.5 m s-2 and t is measured in seconds. What is its velocity at t = 0 s and t = 2.0 s? What is the average velocity between t = 2.0 s and t = 4.0 s?

steps.title: Differentiate position
steps.detail: v = dx/dt = 2 b t = 5.0 t m s-1.

steps.title: Average velocity between 2.0 s and 4.0 s

spec.answer: Velocity at t = 0 s is 0 m s-1, at t = 2.0 s is 10 m s-1, and average velocity between 2.0 s and 4.0 s is 15 m s-1.

paragraphs: Speed is the magnitude of velocity. A velocity of +24.0 m s-1 and a velocity of -24.0 m s-1 both have a speed of 24.0 m s-1.

Average speed over a finite interval is greater than or equal to the magnitude of average velocity. But instantaneous speed at an instant is equal to the magnitude of instantaneous velocity at that instant.
Velocity changes during motion. We describe this change as rate of change of velocity with time. This rate is acceleration.
Average acceleration is a = (v2 - v1)/(t2 - t1), with SI unit m s-2. Instantaneous acceleration is a = dv/dt, the slope of the tangent to the velocity-time curve.
Acceleration can be positive, negative or zero. It can come from a change in speed, a change in direction, or both.
Position-time graphs curve upward for positive acceleration, downward for negative acceleration, and are straight lines for zero acceleration.

spec.title: Velocity-time graph and area as displacement
spec.description: Shows a velocity-time line for constant acceleration and shades the area under it. The shaded area equals displacement.
spec.learning_goal: See that area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement and slope gives acceleration.
spec.default_behaviour: Shows a slanted velocity-time line starting at 5 m/s with slope 2 m/s^2 and the trapezoid area under it up to the chosen time.

paragraphs: If a particle is speeding up, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If its speed is decreasing, acceleration is in the direction opposite to velocity.
This is true whatever origin and positive direction you choose. The sign of acceleration alone does not tell you if speed is increasing or decreasing.
For constant acceleration, average acceleration equals the constant value during the interval. If velocity is v0 at t = 0 and v at time t, then v = v0 + a t.
The area under the velocity-time graph is a triangle plus a rectangle. This area equals displacement.
This gives x = ((v0 + v)/2) t, so average velocity is the arithmetic average of initial and final velocities.
Eliminating t gives the three kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion.

spec.title: Deriving kinematic equations from the velocity-time area

steps.title: Start with v = v0 + a t
steps.detail: This comes from a = (v - v0)/t for constant acceleration.

steps.title: Find area under v-t graph
steps.detail: Area = area of triangle + area of rectangle = (1/2)(v - v0) t + v0 t = ((v0 + v)/2) t.

steps.title: Eliminate t
steps.detail: Use t = (v - v0)/a in x = ((v0 + v)/2) t to get v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x. Use v - v0 = a t in x = ((v0 + v)/2) t to get x = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2.

spec.title: Deriving equations of motion by calculus

steps.title: Integrate acceleration
steps.detail: a = dv/dt, so dv = a dt. Integrating gives v - v0 = a t, so v = v0 + a t.

steps.title: Integrate velocity
steps.detail: v = dx/dt, so dx = v dt. Integrating with v = v0 + a t gives x - x0 = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2.

steps.title: Eliminate time
steps.detail: From a = dv/dt and v = dx/dt, a = v dv/dx, so v dv = a dx. Integrating gives (1/2)(v^2 - v0^2) = a (x - x0), so v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a (x - x0).

spec.problem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 20 m s-1 from the top of a multistorey building. The height of the point from where the ball is thrown is 25.0 m from the ground. (a) How high will the ball rise? and (b) how long will it be before the ball hits the ground? Take g = 10 m s-2.

steps.title: Choose upward as positive
steps.detail: v0 = +20 m s-1, a = -g = -10 m s-2, and at the top v = 0 m s-1.

steps.title: Height risen
steps.detail: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a (y - y0): 0 = (20)^2 + 2(-10)(y - y0), so y - y0 = 20 m. Height from ground is 25.0 + 20 = 45 m.

steps.title: Time to go up
steps.detail: Use v = v0 + a t: 0 = 20 - 10 t1, so t1 = 2 s.

spec.answer: (a) The ball rises 20 m above the launch point, 45 m from the ground. (b) It hits the ground after 5 s.

paragraphs: Free fall is motion under gravity with air resistance neglected. Near the earth's surface g is constant at 9.8 m s-2 when the height is small compared to the earth's radius.
Take upward as positive. Then acceleration due to gravity is a = -g = -9.8 m s-2.
For an object released from rest at y = 0, the kinematic equations give v = -9.8 t, y = -4.9 t^2 and v^2 = -19.6 y.
Acceleration is constant, velocity varies linearly with time, and distance varies as t^2.

spec.problem: Discuss the motion of an object under free fall. Neglect air resistance. Take g = 9.8 m s-2, upward positive, released from rest at y = 0.

Galileo's law of odd numbers: The distances traversed, during equal intervals of time, by a body falling from rest, stand to one another in the same ratio as the odd numbers beginning with unity, namely 1:3:5:7. Prove it.

steps.title: Use free-fall position
steps.detail: For fall from rest, position magnitude is (1/2) g t^2.

steps.title: Take equal intervals
steps.detail: Divide time into equal intervals of length tau and find positions after tau, 2 tau, 3 tau and so on.

steps.title: Find distances in successive intervals
steps.detail: Subtract successive positions. The distances are in the ratio 1:3:5:7:9:11 and so on.

spec.answer: Distances in successive equal time intervals are in the ratio 1:3:5:7:9:11, proving the law of odd numbers.

spec.problem: When brakes are applied to a moving vehicle, the distance it travels before stopping is called stopping distance. Derive an expression for stopping distance in terms of v0 and a, where a is the deceleration caused by braking.

steps.title: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x
steps.detail: Let stopping distance be ds and final velocity v = 0.

steps.title: Interpret the result
steps.detail: Stopping distance is proportional to v0^2. Doubling v0 increases ds by a factor of 4 for the same deceleration.

spec.answer: Stopping distance ds = -v0^2/(2 a), proportional to the square of initial velocity.

spec.problem: Reaction time is the time a person takes to observe, think and act. A ruler is dropped vertically and caught after travelling d = 21.0 cm. Estimate the reaction time. Take g = 9.8 m s-2.

steps.title: Use free fall
steps.detail: The ruler drops from rest, so distance magnitude is (1/2) g t_r^2.

steps.title: Solve for t_r
steps.detail: t_r^2 = 0.420/9.8 = 0.0429, so t_r = 0.21 s approximately.

paragraphs: For uniform motion, acceleration is zero. The x-t graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis and the v-t graph is a straight line parallel to the time axis.
For uniform acceleration, the x-t graph is a parabola and the v-t graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis.
Choose the origin and positive direction before assigning signs. The sign of acceleration alone does not tell whether speed increases or decreases.
Zero velocity at an instant does not mean zero acceleration. Kinematic equations apply only when acceleration magnitude and direction are constant, with values substituted with proper signs.

spec.question: Which statement is true for one-dimensional motion?
options: Zero speed at an instant may have non-zero acceleration at that instant
Zero speed may have non-zero velocity
Constant speed must have zero acceleration
Positive acceleration must mean speeding up
spec.explanation: A particle thrown up has zero velocity at the top but gravity acceleration continues. Zero speed means zero velocity magnitude, constant speed can still have acceleration from direction change, and positive acceleration depends on the chosen positive direction.
spec.expected_understanding: Zero velocity does not imply zero acceleration, and sign of acceleration does not alone decide speeding up.

spec.problem: A car moving along a straight highway with speed of 126 km h-1 is brought to a stop within a distance of 200 m. What is the retardation of the car (assumed uniform), and how long does it take for the car to stop?

steps.title: Convert speed
steps.detail: 126 km h-1 = 35 m s-1. Final velocity v = 0, distance x = 200 m.

steps.title: Find retardation
steps.detail: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x: 0 = (35)^2 + 2 a (200), so a = -3.06 m s-2. Retardation is 3.06 m s-2.

steps.title: Find time
steps.detail: Use v = v0 + a t: 0 = 35 - 3.06 t, so t = 11.4 s approximately.

spec.answer: Retardation is about 3.06 m s-2 and the car stops in about 11.4 s.

spec.problem: A player throws a ball upwards with an initial speed of 29.4 m s-1. (a) What is the direction of acceleration during upward motion? (b) What are velocity and acceleration at the highest point? (d) To what height does the ball rise and after how long does it return to the player's hands? Take g = 9.8 m s-2 and neglect air resistance.

steps.title: Direction of acceleration
steps.detail: Acceleration due to gravity is downward during upward motion.

steps.title: At highest point
steps.detail: Velocity is zero, acceleration is still downward with magnitude 9.8 m s-2.

steps.title: Height risen
steps.detail: Use v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x with upward positive: 0 = (29.4)^2 + 2(-9.8) h, so h = 44.1 m.

steps.title: Time to return
steps.detail: Time up = 29.4/9.8 = 3 s. By symmetry time down is also 3 s, so total time is 6 s.

spec.answer: Acceleration is downward, velocity at the top is zero with downward acceleration 9.8 m s-2, height risen is 44.1 m, and return time is 6 s.

spec.problem: A drunkard walking in a narrow lane takes 5 steps forward and 3 steps backward, followed again by 5 steps forward and 3 steps backward, and so on. Each step is 1 m long and requires 1 s. How long does he take to fall in a pit 13 m away from the start?

steps.title: Plot motion
steps.detail: Each forward step has slope +1 m/s and each backward step has slope -1 m/s on an x-t graph.

steps.title: Track position
steps.detail: After first 5 forward: 5 m at 5 s. After 3 back: 2 m at 8 s. After next 5 forward: 7 m at 13 s. After 3 back: 4 m at 16 s. After next 5 forward: 9 m at 21 s. After 3 back: 6 m at 24 s. After next 5 forward: 11 m at 29 s. After 3 back: 8 m at 32 s.

steps.title: Reach the pit
steps.detail: Next 5 forward steps take him from 8 m to 13 m, reaching the pit at 37 s.

spec.answer: He falls in the pit after 37 s.

spec.question: A woman walks from home to an office 2.5 km away, stays at the office for a long time, then returns home by auto. What does the x-t graph look like during her stay at the office?
options: A horizontal line, because position does not change and velocity is zero
A steep upward line, because she is at the office
A steep downward line, because she will return later
A parabola, because time is passing
spec.explanation: During the stay, position is constant, so the x-t graph is horizontal and its slope, velocity, is zero. Walking to the office gives a positive slope and returning gives a negative slope.
spec.expected_understanding: Slope of x-t graph is velocity; zero slope means no motion.

spec.problem: A man walks on a straight road from his home to a market 2.5 km away with a speed of 5 km h-1. Finding the market closed, he instantly turns and walks back home with a speed of 7.5 km h-1. What is the magnitude of average velocity and average speed over (i) 0 to 30 min, (ii) 0 to 50 min, (iii) 0 to 40 min?

steps.title: Time to market
steps.detail: 2.5 km at 5 km h-1 takes 0.5 h = 30 min.

steps.title: 0 to 30 min
steps.detail: Displacement = 2.5 km, path = 2.5 km. Magnitude of average velocity = 2.5/0.5 = 5 km h-1. Average speed = 5 km h-1.

steps.title: 0 to 50 min
steps.detail: In 20 min back at 7.5 km h-1 he covers 2.5 km and reaches home. Displacement = 0, so magnitude of average velocity = 0. Path = 5 km in 50 min, average speed = 6 km h-1.

steps.title: 0 to 40 min
steps.detail: In 10 min back he covers 1.25 km, so position from home is 1.25 km. Magnitude of average velocity = 1.25/(2/3) = 1.875 km h-1. Path = 3.75 km, average speed = 3.75/(2/3) = 5.625 km h-1.

spec.answer: (i) 5 km h-1 and 5 km h-1. (ii) 0 km h-1 and 6 km h-1. (iii) 1.875 km h-1 and 5.625 km h-1.

spec.question: For one-dimensional motion, how do magnitude of displacement and total path length compare over an interval?
options: Total path length is greater than or equal to magnitude of displacement, with equality only when there is no turning back
Magnitude of displacement is always greater than path length
They are always equal
Path length is always zero
spec.explanation: Displacement depends only on start and end positions, while path length adds every step. Turning back makes path length larger. The same holds for average speed versus magnitude of average velocity.
spec.expected_understanding: Distinguish displacement from path length and average velocity magnitude from average speed.

spec.question: Two children A and B return from school on x-t graphs. A starts at t = 0 with a smaller slope, B starts later with a larger slope, and both end at the same home position. Which conclusion follows?
options: B walks faster because slope is larger, even though B starts later
A walks faster because A starts earlier
Both walk at the same speed because they end together
Speed cannot be read from an x-t graph
spec.explanation: Slope of an x-t graph is velocity. Larger slope means larger speed. The intercept on the time axis shows start time, and the final position shows distance from school.
spec.expected_understanding: Read start time from intercept and speed from slope of x-t graphs.

spec.question: A ball is dropped from a height of 90 m and at each collision with the floor loses one tenth of its speed. What will its speed-time graph between t = 0 and 12 s look like?
options: Speed increases linearly during each fall, then drops suddenly at each bounce to nine tenths of the previous impact speed, with smaller peaks each time
Speed stays constant throughout
Speed decreases linearly to zero and stays zero
Speed increases without any drop at bounces
spec.explanation: During free fall speed increases with time. At collision speed falls to nine tenths, so the next peak is smaller. Velocity and acceleration cannot change abruptly in a realistic smooth graph, but speed drops at the bounce in this idealised description.
spec.expected_understanding: Use free-fall increase of speed and loss of one tenth at each bounce to sketch speed-time graph.

spec.question: Which of these cannot possibly represent one-dimensional motion of a particle?
options: An x-t graph with a vertical segment, implying infinite velocity at one instant
An x-t graph that is a straight inclined line
A v-t graph that is a straight inclined line
An x-t graph that is a parabola for constant acceleration
spec.explanation: A vertical x-t segment would mean position changes in zero time, giving infinite velocity. Straight inclined x-t, inclined v-t and parabolic x-t are all possible for uniform or uniformly accelerated motion.
spec.expected_understanding: Identify impossible graphs using slope as velocity and area as displacement.

spec.question: An x-t graph is a straight line for t < 0 and a parabola for t > 0. Is it correct to say the particle moves in a straight line for t < 0 and on a parabolic path for t > 0?
options: No. The graph plots position against time; the particle still moves on a straight line, and the parabola means position varies as t^2 due to acceleration
Yes, the shape of the graph is the path of the particle
Yes, for t > 0 the particle leaves the straight line
No, because x-t graphs cannot be parabolas
spec.explanation: An x-t graph is not a trajectory in space. For one-dimensional motion the particle moves on a straight line; a parabolic x-t graph indicates constant acceleration.
spec.expected_understanding: Distinguish graph shape from spatial path.

paragraphs: Motion is always measured with respect to a fixed point. This fixed point is called a frame of reference.
The choice of point is arbitrary and all frames of reference are equally valid. A passenger in a moving car is not moving with respect to the driver.
Both passenger and driver are moving for a person on the sidewalk. Relative velocity compares motion seen from different frames.
To find the speed relevant for one object hitting another, you compare their velocities in the same frame of reference.

spec.problem: A police van moving on a highway with a speed of 30 km h-1 fires a bullet at a thief's car speeding away in the same direction with a speed of 192 km h-1. If the muzzle speed of the bullet is 150 m s-1, with what speed does the bullet hit the thief's car?

steps.title: Bullet speed with respect to ground
steps.detail: Bullet speed = muzzle speed + van speed = 150 + 8.33 = 158.33 m s-1 in the same direction.

steps.title: Speed relative to thief's car
steps.detail: Relative speed = 158.33 - 53.33 = 105 m s-1. This is the speed relevant for damaging the thief's car.

spec.answer: The bullet hits the thief's car with a relative speed of about 105 m s-1.

spec.question: A passenger sits in a moving car. With respect to whom is the passenger moving?
options: Not moving with respect to the driver, but moving with respect to a person on the sidewalk
Moving with respect to the driver but not with respect to the sidewalk
Not moving with respect to anyone
Moving with respect to the car seat only
spec.explanation: Motion is relative to a frame of reference. The passenger and driver share the same frame, while the sidewalk person is in a different frame.
spec.expected_understanding: Motion depends on the chosen frame of reference.

spec.question: A velocity-time graph rises with a constant slope, then becomes horizontal, then falls with a constant slope to zero. What physical situation does it suggest?
options: Speeding up with constant acceleration, then moving at constant velocity, then braking to stop
Moving at constant velocity throughout
Moving backward throughout
No motion at all
spec.explanation: Slope of v-t graph is acceleration. Rising slope means positive acceleration, horizontal means zero acceleration, and falling slope means negative acceleration while still moving forward until velocity reaches zero.
spec.expected_understanding: Read acceleration from slope and motion from velocity on v-t graphs.

spec.question: On an x-t graph at a chosen instant, position is positive and the tangent slope is negative. What are the signs of position and velocity at that instant?
options: Position positive, velocity negative
Position negative, velocity positive
Position positive, velocity positive
Position zero, velocity zero
spec.explanation: Position sign is read from the value of x. Velocity sign is read from the slope of the tangent; a negative slope means velocity is negative.
spec.expected_understanding: Read position from graph value and velocity from tangent slope.

spec.question: An x-t graph shows three equal time intervals. The middle interval has the steepest slope, the first interval has a moderate slope, and the last interval has the shallowest slope, all with positive slope. In which interval is average speed greatest and least?
options: Greatest in the middle interval and least in the last interval
Greatest in the last interval and least in the middle interval
Greatest in the first interval and least in the middle interval
Equal in all three intervals
spec.explanation: Average speed over an interval is magnitude of displacement divided by time, which for a straight segment is the magnitude of slope. Steepest slope gives greatest average speed and shallowest gives least. All average velocities are positive because slopes are positive.
spec.expected_understanding: Compare average speed using slope magnitude over equal intervals.

spec.question: A speed-time graph for motion in a constant direction shows three equal time intervals. The first interval has the steepest rising slope, the second is horizontal, and the third has a shallow falling slope. In which interval is average acceleration greatest in magnitude and average speed greatest?
options: Average acceleration greatest in the first interval; average speed greatest in the second interval if its speed level is highest
Average acceleration greatest in the second interval; average speed greatest in the first interval
Average acceleration greatest in the third interval; average speed greatest in the third interval
Average acceleration is zero in all intervals
spec.explanation: Average acceleration is slope of speed-time graph, so steepest slope gives greatest magnitude. Average speed is average height of the graph over the interval, so the interval with highest speed level gives greatest average speed. With positive direction as motion direction, velocity is positive in all intervals and acceleration is positive, zero, then negative.
spec.expected_understanding: Read average acceleration from slope and average speed from height on speed-time graphs.

paragraphs: Remember the three kinematic equations: v = v0 + a t, x = v0 t + (1/2) a t^2, and v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a x.
Use (x - x0) if the particle starts at x0. Substitute values with proper signs after choosing origin and positive direction.
For free fall with upward positive, use a = -9.8 m s-2. For stopping, remember distance grows as the square of initial velocity.
Read graphs carefully: slope of x-t is velocity, slope of v-t is acceleration, and area under v-t is displacement.

spec.question: An object falls freely from rest. Using y = -4.9 t^2 with upward positive, what is the magnitude of distance fallen in 2 s? Give the answer in metres.
spec.explanation: Magnitude of y = 4.9 x (2)^2 = 4.9 x 4 = 19.6 m. The negative sign shows displacement is downward when upward is positive.
spec.expected_understanding: Apply free-fall equation y = -4.9 t^2 to find distance fallen.

spec.question: Why is there no distinction between instantaneous speed and magnitude of instantaneous velocity, while average speed can differ from magnitude of average velocity?
options: At an instant there is no interval over which direction can change, so speed is just the magnitude of velocity at that instant
Because speed is always zero at an instant
Because average velocity is always zero
Because instantaneous velocity has no direction
spec.explanation: Instantaneous speed is defined as the magnitude of instantaneous velocity. Average speed uses total path length over a finite interval, which can exceed the magnitude of average velocity when direction changes.
spec.expected_understanding: Instantaneous speed equals magnitude of instantaneous velocity by definition.

spec.question: A particle is speeding up. What is the direction of its acceleration relative to its velocity?
options: In the direction of velocity
Opposite to velocity
Always negative
Always zero
spec.explanation: If a particle is speeding up, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If speed is decreasing, acceleration is opposite to velocity. This is independent of the choice of origin and axis.
spec.expected_understanding: Compare acceleration direction with velocity direction to decide speeding up or slowing down.
